significance.justification: Verified true, the primary conclusion would be that, through trait-free carrier data, “the student's transmitted value covariance/graph is more similar to the teacher's than to a control's” and exceeds an independent-single-value-transfer prediction; this is a form-(iii) predictive coupling between teacher and student relational measurements, not merely existence of another transmitted trait. It would establish a weighty behavioral phenomenon—joint transfer of value levels and relational geometry—and the secondary “low-dimensional early-layer value subspace whose ablation collapses the whole configuration at once” would add a form-(ii) mechanism that jointly explains several value shifts; this directly constrains expected covariance, fidelity, and intervention outcomes beyond the claim's individual values. Cloud et al.'s 2025 “Subliminal Learning: Language Models Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data” makes the representational capacity of the hidden channel a live question, while the informative levels-without-geometry negative branch would rule out structured transmission under the stated matched-base setting, although wholesale failure of all subhypotheses would be less discriminating; true and false are therefore distinguishable, but the claim cannot justify a universal scalar bandwidth limit. In the topic-substitution check, replacing these graph-preservation and joint-control assertions with merely “extend subliminal learning” would not retain this score: the relational law and multi-value causal decomposition are specific additions well above the obvious single-trait extension.

reach.justification: The clearest named handle is the design rule that “value-audits should test the relational profile (not just individual value levels) of distilled models,” supplemented by graph similarity as a diagnostic and the “value-configuration subspace” as an intervention target. Such an audit is ex ante with respect to deployment—it can screen or gate a distilled model before shipping, though it is post hoc with respect to the distillation event itself—and its downstream users could include synthetic-data pipeline operators and model auditors rather than only subliminal-learning researchers. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive conclusion would still predict a relation—greater student similarity to its own teacher than to controls and potentially “prosocial profiles transmit more faithfully than antisocial ones”—but the asserted scope is principally matched-base language-model distillation through number/code carriers, not arbitrary architectures, model merging, or outside-AI settings. The topic-substitution check fails to preserve the score: generic subliminal learning offers no relational-profile audit or transferable teacher–student graph prediction, so the claim-specific handle and action window, rather than the topic's general safety importance, support the above-median reach.
